Pays Plat First Nation

Pays Plat First Nation’s public history connects the community with the north shore of Lake Superior and the name Pawgwasheeng. These starting readings pair that community account with a September2026 announcement about land for future housing and development, keeping historical interpretation and dated administrative reporting distinct.

01

Names and infrastructure history

Pays Plat’s public history explains the French name as flat land and gives Pawgwasheeng as a name referring to shallow water. The same account describes railway, highway and hydro corridors cutting through the community and links those pressures with efforts to obtain a larger land base. These are the Nation’s own historical interpretations. The page’s older statement that a final agreement was still being drafted must be distinguished from later announcements.

Read the sources [1] Pays Plat First Nation

02

A September2026 milestone

A joint release dated September23,2026 announces a4,203-acre addition to Pays Plat’s reserve and describes it as implementing a2018 Land and Larger Land Base agreement. Chief David Mushquash frames the expansion around housing, youth, Elders and members’ hopes of returning. The release provides a dated administrative milestone and community priorities; it does not establish that every proposed home or economic project has already been built.

Read the sources [2] Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada; joint release distributed by Cision

Our Community: Our History ↗

Read the complete Our Community and Our History body. The Nation explains Pays Plat and Pawgwasheeng, recounts railway and infrastructure pressures and presents its oral-history account of treaty non-signing. Its older agreement-status wording is not adopted as current; underlying trader records, treaty instruments and oral-history recordings were not inspected.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete main community/history body; synthesis selects public place-name and infrastructure history, not unverified universal first-record claims or legal conclusions.

Pays Plat First Nation marks milestone with new addition to reserve lands ↗

Publication: 2026-09-23

The September23,2026 release identifies its federal, provincial and First Nation participants and announces a4,203-acre reserve addition implementing a2018 agreement. Read the main body and named participants’ quotations. Housing, economic development and returning members are stated goals; no completed construction, present legal advice or settlement of every claim is inferred.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Read the main release dated September23,2026, introductory institutional attribution and quotations through the community Chief’s statement; no review of underlying2018 agreement or transfer instruments.
